title: Cifrario of Cosimo I's chancery with don Bernardino de Mendoza at Naples, 10 September 1555
correspondents: Cosimo I's chancery <-> don Bernardino de Mendoza (Naples)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo del Principato 448, c. 277
folio_note: One leaf headed "1555 ... Con il S. Don Ber.no di Mendozza a Napoli": alphabet with one or two figure values per letter, nulls, and a nomenclator in three columns numbered to about 900 (Papa, Imperatore, Re, Francesi, Siena, Roma, Napoli, Milano, Piombino, Orbetello ...). Inventory vol. VIII p. 41 and index: "cifrario usato a Napoli con Bernardino de Mendoza, 1555 settembre 10, 448, 277".
status: Key only. Not checked against any letter; Mendoza's Naples letters of 1555-57 in filze 448-460 are the place to look.
why: A dated key of the Siena-war chancery: any bare Mendoza letter in Mediceo 448-470 can be read with it.
verify: Transcribe the table; search filze 448-470 (vol. VIII-IX inventory) for Mendoza letters in cipher.
source: ASF Mediceo del Principato, Carteggio universale (PAD images) + Carteggio universale di Cosimo I inventory PDFs (ASF Inventari on-line), second ASF Florence pass, Nov 2026
score_note: Scored from the images viewed during the second ASF Florence pass, 6 Nov 2026 (research/sweep_2026-11_asf_florence_2/)

title: Cipher letter of 24 August 1481 with its own letter-by-letter interlinear decipherment (digits and Greek-like signs)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 172 (old c. 204)
folio_note: One small leaf: two clear lines, then about six lines of cipher in digits and Greek-like signs with a clear letter written over each sign; dated "xxiiii augusti 1481". MAP inventory vol. 3: "... 1481 ago. 24, n. 172".
status: Key source (glossed), flagged by vetting batch n10. Its digits-plus-Greek style recalls key sheet LXXII 179 (ser Andrea da Bologna: a-g = 1-9, h-y Greek letters) and lead 2310 (LXXII 213-214).
why: A worked example of a 1481 Medici cipher: the sign values can be read directly and tested on lead 2310 and on key sheet 179.
verify: Transcribe sign/letter pairs; compare with key sheet 179 and the slips of lead 2310.

why: Confirms or completes the Alamanni key (178) and gives the key for any bare Alamanni letter of 1489-92 in MAP.

title: Partial cipher alphabet on a strip filed as LXXII doc. 189 bis
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 189 bis
folio_note: A narrow strip: the alphabet a-x in one line with one to three cipher values under some letters (+, II, C under a; m, f, circled-dot signs, 7, 8, a division sign, pi, 6, 9, o, p and q-like signs under others).
status: Key fragment only; filed after Bibbiena's 1512 letter (doc. 189), whose signs it does not obviously match.
why: A small key that may belong to one of the bare sign-cipher letters of LXXII or LXXIII.
verify: Compare with the sign sets of LXXII 189, 196-211 and leads 2310-2311.

title: Cipher slip LXXII 209 with its clear decipherment 210 (Bernardo Rucellai, 1482), a second Rucellai system
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, docs. 209-210 (old cc. 252-253)
folio_note: 209: an oblong slip of about 17 lines of dense signs (slashes, crosses, digits, Greek-like letters), no clear word; 210: a clear text of matching length (vetting n10). Inventory: "Bernardo Rucellai, or(ator). Mediolani, 1482 lug. 12, n. 175; ago. 27, n. 203; mar. 28, n. 209".
status: Read by its filed decipherment (210); key material. Its sign set differs from the 196-207 Rucellai system.
why: Gives a second Rucellai table of 1482 for any bare letter in that system.
verify: Align 209 with 210 and record the table.

title: Twelve key sheets of Lorenzo de' Medici's chancery, MAP CXIX 115-125 and 127 (Urbino, Calabria, Tornabuoni, Soderini, Lodovico Sforza, Piero de' Medici, Costanzo Sforza, Mortellas, Centurioni, Pellegrino da Forlì, Ranuccio Farnese)
correspondents: Lorenzo de' Medici's chancery <-> the duke of Urbino, the duke of Calabria, Giovanni Tornabuoni, the Venetian ambassador, Paolantonio Soderini, Lodovico Sforza, Piero de' Medici, Costanzo Sforza, Dionigi Mortellas, Giovan Battista Centurioni, Pellegrino (Rossi) da Forlì, Ranuccio (Farnese) (per the inventory, not matched sheet by sheet)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXIX, docs. 115-125, 127 (old cc. 116-126, 128)
folio_note: 115 (c. 116, with blank 116 bis): alphabet with three values, nulls, doubles, nomenclator (Papa, Re de Sicilia, Signoria de Genova, Duca de Milano, Fiorentini, Duca de Ferrara, Duca de Urbino, Conte Hieronymo, Roberto Malatesta, Costanzo, Signore de Faenza ...), so c. 1478-82; 116 (c. 117; 117 bis a list of sign words: Arcadi, Danari, Gente d'arme, Fanti, Vettovaglia, Alloggiamenti ...) "Cum duca Calabriae 1485": alphabet, doubles, "Nihil importantes", nomenclator (Papa, Re, Duca di Calabria, Cardinals Orsini, Savello, Colonna, Duca d'Andria, Fabrizio Colonna ...); 117: alphabet, doubles, nulls, long nomenclator, pencil "1492-1498"; 118: alphabet, nulls, doubles, numbered nomenclator 20-54 (Veneziani, Duce, Turco, Armata, Papa, Re Ferrando ...); 119: alphabet with three values, doubles, nulls, long nomenclator; 120: small alphabet and numbered names (Papa, S. Francesco, Lorenzo ... Cardinali); 121: alphabet, doubles, nulls and particles; 122: alphabet over a short covering letter ("ho fatta la cifra per potervi meglio informare ..."); 123: alphabet with homophones and a two-column nomenclator (Roma, Napoli, Venezia, Re di Spagna, Genova, Savona, Spinola, Fregosi, Adorni ...); 124: alphabet and a few names (Siena, Bentivoglio?, Ducati, Roma, Milano, Napoli, Veneziani, Duca di Ferrara); 125: alphabet with homophones, doubles, "nihil importantes" phrases, nomenclator; 127 "Cum ... Ranuccio": alphabet with digits and a numbered nomenclator (Papa, Cardinali, Roma, Conte Hieronymo, Duca di Calabria ...). 126 is a cipher text (row in candidates.json).
status: Keys only; individual attribution to the inventory's twelve names not done (only 116 Calabria 1485 and 127 Ranuccio are endorsed legibly at 900 px). None tested yet.
why: With LXXII 178-188, the second Laurentian key set: first test for CXIX 126 and for the bare MAP letters (leads 2309-2311, 2320-2324 and the LXXII rows of this pass).
verify: Transcribe each table at full size (1600 px); attribute each to the inventory names; match sign sets against CXIX 126 and the bare MAP letters.
